title: September-October warmth gave no clear common link to ginkgo autumn intervals at 35 Japan stations in 1953-2025
abstract: We tested whether September-October warmth changed the time from ginkgo yellowing to leaf fall. We used 2,202 paired station-years at 35 Japan stations in 1953-2025. Four separate North and South, early and late models removed station and year effects. Slopes ranged from -1.55 to +2.97 days per C. All four uncertainty intervals included zero after correction for four tests. Station trends, observation-code selection and alternative temperature windows gave the same broad result. The signs did not repeat across periods within either region. This does not show that the interval is constant. Selected complete records, tree and site changes, missing visit logs, current coordinate matching, coarse weather and few station clusters limit inference. We do not identify pollution or causal climate-change effects. The package preserves code, paired dates, a weather panel, source hashes, all estimates, a figure and independent numerical checks.

display.caption: Four separate interval slopes with approximate 95% family coverage across the four tests. All intervals include zero. Negative slopes indicate shorter gaps in warm autumns.

citations.reason: Prior ginkgo budding and leaf-coloring study in Japan; our outcome is the yellowing-to-leaf-fall interval.
Prior campaign paired spring-event study; motivates a distinct autumn test in another observation network. No biological rows are reused.
